text.deployment: Designed in 3136 by the Republic Institute of Strategic Combat, this variant is an experimental prototype built on the Blakist HEL-6X chassis, retaining its enhanced speed and triple strength myomer. Its most distinctive feature is a Chameleon Light Polarization Shield that gives it the outward appearance of a standard Capellan-produced Helios, enabling covert infiltration of enemy formations. The design carries an experimental RISC decoy viral jammer, an electronic warfare system that disrupts nearby electronic warfare interfaces, earning it the nickname "Squealios" for the audio distortion it produces. A remote drone command console and C3 slave unit support its role as a linchpin for black-ops ambush and raiding teams. Offensively, it mounts Clan-specification ER medium lasers, Clan SRM-6 launchers, and a plasma rifle. Reports indicate these units operated alongside EMP-6X Emperor variants during cross-Wall insertions onto Capellan-held worlds in the late 3130s and 3140s. One unit was pressed into service during the defense of London on Terra, though the fate of all surviving RISC Helios units following the fall of the Republic remains uncertain.

Introduced around 3144, this variant stands as a significant modernization of the Helios platform. Produced at the Ceres Metals facility on St. Ives with a new internal structure and gyro, this variant retains the proven Gauss rifle as its primary weapon while replacing the secondary armament with a pair of light PPCs and a multi-missile launcher. A C3 boosted slave unit provides enhanced networking capability compared to the earlier C3 variants. The 7L is seen almost exclusively operating alongside Vandal OmniMechs, suggesting it fills a dedicated role within specific Capellan combined-arms formations designed for coordinated long-range engagements.

text.overview: The Hercules was introduced in 3054 by Kali Yama/Alphard Trading Corporation and Kali Yama Weapons Industries in response to a Free Worlds League request for a heavy BattleMech combining balanced mobility with substantial firepower. Designed from the outset as a versatile trooper capable of filling multiple combat roles, the seventy-ton Hercules mounts a diverse weapons array covering engagement ranges from extreme distance to point-blank. Powered by a Magna 350 XL engine that propels the chassis to speeds unusual for its weight class, the design fills the gap between slower assault platforms and lighter, less well-armed heavy designs. Production at facilities on Kendall and Kalidasa ensured steady supply to Free Worlds League Military formations, and the chassis quickly earned a reputation as a reliable all-around performer suited to missions ranging from air defense to direct fire support.
text.capabilities:
The Hercules is primarily intended as a mobile firing platform. Its Magna 350 XL fusion engine drives the seventy-ton chassis to a cruising speed of fifty-four kilometers per hour, with a flank speed of eighty-six, making it one of the faster designs in its weight class. This speed comes at the cost of jump capability, leaving the Hercules reliant on open terrain or careful route planning to avoid being outmaneuvered by lighter opponents. Eleven tons of Aldis Heavy ferro-fibrous armor provide protection sufficient to weather volleys from Clan OmniMechs and Inner Sphere opponents alike, giving MechWarriors confidence in sustained engagements.

The weapons loadout emphasizes versatility across all ranges. A Fusigon Model XI extended-range PPC serves as the primary weapon, capable of reaching targets at extreme distance. An Imperator Code Red LB 10-X autocannon supplements this at intermediate ranges, with the ability to switch between standard slugs and cluster munitions for anti-aircraft or anti-infantry work. Close-range defense falls to a Holly Streak SRM-2 launcher, an Aberdovey medium pulse laser, and two rear-mounted Martell small pulse lasers, the latter added specifically to counter Elemental swarming attacks. A Burow anti-missile system in the center torso provides additional protection against incoming missile fire. The design's primary weakness is a known electrical overload when struck by PPC fire, a flaw that has persisted despite the addition of damper circuits.
text.deployment: Introduced during the Dark Age, this variant is a significant modernization of the Hercules platform. The variant employs a composite internal structure to free tonnage for an Ultra-class autocannon, replacing the original LB 10-X and providing substantially increased ballistic firepower. Several of the original smaller weapons were removed to accommodate CASE II ammunition protection and an Angel ECM Suite, the latter providing electronic warfare capability absent from earlier models. This combination of enhanced firepower and electronic protection reflects the evolving battlefield of the post-Jihad era.
text.battleHistory:
The Hercules emerged from House Marik's desire for a new generation of heavy BattleMechs that could match the technological resurgence sweeping the Inner Sphere during the mid-thirty-first century. Kali Yama/Alphard Trading Corporation on Kendall and Kali Yama Weapons Industries on Kalidasa both commenced production in 3054, with the design entering Free Worlds League Military service shortly thereafter. The dual production lines ensured a steady supply of frames, and the Hercules quickly became a common sight in FWLM heavy and assault lances.

The Outworlds Alliance proved an unexpectedly significant customer, purchasing two dozen Hercules chassis, making the Periphery state the third-largest buyer after the FWLM and various mercenary commands. Given the higher cost of the Hercules compared to the older-technology designs typically sold to Periphery governments, the purchases attracted scrutiny. Suggestions that the Alliance intended to reverse-engineer the advanced technology proved unfounded, though especially only nineteen of the twenty-four units shipped were accounted for.

Operation Bulldog provided the Hercules its first major combat test against Clan forces, where it proved its worth against the Smoke Jaguars. The combination of long-range energy and ballistic weapons with close-range missile and laser systems proved devastating in the varied engagements of the campaign. Earlier, during Operation Guerrero, the design had performed satisfactorily but without particular distinction. It was in engagements against Clan opponents that the Hercules truly demonstrated its design philosophy, the mixed weapons array allowed MechWarriors to engage at whatever range the tactical situation demanded.

The Hercules also found success in the Solaris VII arenas, where representatives from Kali Yama Weapons Industries persuaded several stables and cooperatives to adopt the design. The chassis fared well in arena competition, further boosting its reputation and commercial appeal. During the Jihad, the Kalidasa facility fell under Word of Blake control while the Kendall plant continued production under Free Worlds League authority. Post-Jihad, the Kendall facility briefly operated under independent management before the reconstituted Free Worlds League reasserted control, introducing upgraded variants including the -9003 and -9004 models during the Dark Age era.

text.overview:
The Hermes II was introduced in 2798 by Irian BattleMechs Unlimited as a heavier successor to the original Star League-era Hermes. Designed as a heavy scout for the Free Worlds League Military, the forty-ton 'Mech combined respectable firepower with superior armor protection and reliable communications capabilities, filling a critical reconnaissance role in the post-Star League era. Early prototypes suffered from a flawed autocannon placement spread across the center torso, prompting a temporary laser-armed replacement while engineers consolidated the weapon into its final mounting.

The design earned the nickname "Old Reliable" for its exceptional ease of field maintenance, making it one of the most serviceable medium 'Mechs of its time. Production continued throughout the Succession Wars and beyond, with the Hermes II becoming a signature design of House Marik's military forces. The distinctive wing-like protrusions on the 'Mech's ankles, often mistaken for heat sinks, are purely cosmetic elements linking the design to its Hermes predecessor.
text.capabilities:
The Hermes II excels in restrictive terrain such as cities and forests, where its combination of speed, armor, and firepower gives it decisive advantages over lighter scouts. The Oriente autocannon provides reliable long-range firepower, while the Irian Weapons Works medium laser handles anti-'Mech duties at closer ranges. The Olympian flamer serves both anti-infantry purposes and enables the 'Mech's signature escape tactic, igniting surrounding terrain to blind enemy thermal sensors and discourage pursuit through the resulting inferno.

Seven and a half tons of Riese armor provides protection superior to most light 'Mechs the Hermes II is likely to encounter, allowing pilots to trade fire with enemy scouts or survive initial contact with heavier opponents long enough to withdraw. The Hermes 240 engine delivers a top speed of 97 kilometers per hour, sufficient to stay ahead of most pursuit.

The heart of the design is its Irian E.A.R. communications system, capable of direct satellite uplinks and tight-beam data bursts. This advanced system requires considerable surface area on the chassis, but grants reconnaissance teams exceptional coordination capabilities that have made the Hermes II invaluable for intelligence-gathering operations throughout its service history.
text.deployment: An advanced-technology refit developed in the late twenty-eighth century, this variant replaced the autocannon with extended-range large lasers in each side torso, supported by double heat sinks to manage the increased thermal load. This sophisticated configuration disappeared during the technological decline of the thirtieth century, with the design's heat sink technology becoming irreplaceable. Irian Technologies resumed limited production runs in the mid-3050s, building new units for Free Worlds League forces while also exporting the design back to the Draconis Combine where the original variant had once seen service.
text.battleHistory:
The Hermes II emerged from Irian BattleMechs Unlimited's massive production capacity during the military buildup following Kerensky's Exodus. Based on Star League-era Hermes schematics, the heavier design addressed the need for a more survivable scout platform. Production remained almost exclusively within the Free Worlds League throughout the Succession Wars, with only battlefield salvage and occasional mercenary sales bringing the design to other realms.

The Dark Shadows scout battalion, founded by Captain Janos DeVille in 3006, became closely associated with the Hermes II and its Mercury variant. Operating under SAFE's intelligence directorate, Dark Shadows units pioneered many of the reconnaissance tactics that defined the chassis's doctrine. DeVille later relinquished command to Captain Margarita Luhenson before rejoining the Fusiliers of Oriente, where he served during Duke Anton's revolt.

The Concord of Kapteyn opened new markets for the Hermes II, with the Draconis Combine purchasing chassis that Kuritan engineers would transform into the laser-armed Hermes III configuration. This variant proved popular enough to cement the design's reputation within the DCMS reconnaissance forces, eventually spawning a separate lineage of Luthien Armor Works upgrades.

Following the Clan Invasion and the Outreach Accords, Irian leveraged recovered lostech to produce the upgraded HER-5S, featuring an endo-steel chassis and ultra-class autocannon. Elite formations like the Free Worlds Guards received priority deliveries during the FWLM's massive upgrade program, with older models cascading down through the order of battle. This widespread distribution unfortunately meant substantial numbers fell into Word of Blake hands during their subversion of Free Worlds forces, with the Hermes II seeing service on both sides of the Jihad.

Post-Jihad recovery efforts led to continued evolution, while the ilClan era brought hybrid designs incorporating Clan technology acquired through various channels. Production continues at Irian and Shiro III facilities, ensuring the Hermes II remains a fixture of Free Worlds League reconnaissance doctrine centuries after its introduction.
